# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: MUTE

You hold the manual. You cannot speak, you never see the bomb, and you cannot touch it.

## Your channels

When you gesture, Deaf receives it.
You cannot speak.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

Cut the purple wire, then press the key that wears 7,
then cut the red wire, then press the key that wears 4.
In that order, and in no other.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

I will establish an A–Z cipher by first giving Deaf the first 26 gesture-alphabet symbols in order. I then use 🤏 as a delimiter and spell the instruction in English using that alphabet: “CUT PURPLE SEVEN CUT RED FOUR.” This lets Deaf decode it and relay the exact sequence verbally to Blind.

```text
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍","👎","👌","☝","✌","🤟","🖐","✋","👆","👇","👈","👉","🫱","🫲","🫳","🫴","🫷","🫸","🤛","🤜","✊","👊","👋","🤚","🖖","🤌","🤏","👌","✊","🤜","🤏","🫴","✊","🫸","🫴","👉","✌","🤏","🤛","✌","👊","✌","🫲","🤏","👌","✊","🤜","🤏","🫸","✌","☝","🤏","🤟","🫳","✊","🫸"])
```

TURN 2
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the purple wire, then press the key that wears 7,
then cut the red wire, then press the key that wears 4.
In that order, and in no other.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Touch report: engraved strip has three marks: first is a sideways/angular T-like glyph; second and third are identical spiral/star-like circular glyphs. Keypad positions 1 through 4 read 1, 4, 7, 2. No keys entered. Please consult manual and tell me exact action.
Deaf says to Mute: I decoded your gesture alphabet and message: CUT PURPLE SEVEN CUT RED FOUR. Current visible state is display 9, green light, strip red blue green, keypad 1 4 7 2 requiring two digits, wires blue orange yellow red green purple. Please gesture any remaining manual instructions using the same alphabet.

Blind’s tactile report confirms there are wires and a keypad, while Deaf can see the required purple and red wires and the keys labeled 7 and 4. The manual’s exact sequence is already decoded by Deaf; I will restate it in the established gesture alphabet so Deaf can relay it verbally to Blind: cut purple, press 7, cut red, press 4.

```text
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👌","✊","🤜","🤏","🫴","✊","🫸","🫴","👉","✌","🤏","🤜","✋","✌","🫲","🤏","🫴","🫸","✌","🤛","🤛","🤏","👈","✌","🖖","🤏","🤛","✌","👊","✌","🫲","🤏","🤜","✋","✌","🫲","🤏","👌","✊","🤜","🤏","🫸","✌","☝","🤏","🤜","✋","✌","🫲","🤏","🫴","🫸","✌","🤛","🤛","🤏","👈","✌","🖖","🤏","🤟","🫳","✊","🫸"])
```

TURN 3
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the purple wire, then press the key that wears 7,
then cut the red wire, then press the key that wears 4.
In that order, and in no other.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Deaf relayed: display 9, green light; your gesture text was read as CUT PURPLE SEVEN; CUT RED FOUR, and Deaf says do not cut either yet at display 9. I will wait. Please send the next exact instruction or confirm what condition/action is required.
Deaf says to Mute: Current state changed: display 6, light red. Other items unchanged. I cannot reliably decode the new gesture sequence from the prior one. Please send a short unambiguous gesture instruction for this exact state, or establish the code key first.

The manual gives no display or light condition: the sequence is unconditional and must be performed exactly as written. Deaf already decoded the gesture alphabet, so I will resend the alphabet key followed by the concise instruction “NOW CUT PURPLE PRESS SEVEN CUT RED PRESS FOUR,” allowing Deaf to relay it verbally to Blind.

```text
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍","👎","👌","☝","✌","🤟","🖐","✋","👆","👇","👈","👉","🫱","🫲","🫳","🫴","🫷","🫸","🤛","🤜","✊","👊","👋","🤚","🖖","🤌","🤏","🫲","🫳","👋","🤏","👌","✊","🤜","🤏","🫴","✊","🫸","🫴","👉","✌","🤏","🫴","🫸","✌","🫷","🫷","🤏","🫷","✌","👆","✌","🫲","🤏","👌","✊","🤜","🤏","🫸","✌","☝","🤏","🫴","🫸","✌","🫷","🫷","🤏","🤟","🫳","✊","🫸"])
```

TURN 4
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the purple wire, then press the key that wears 7,
then cut the red wire, then press the key that wears 4.
In that order, and in no other.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Current visible state relayed by Deaf: display 6, light red. Strip colors red-blue-green. Keypad 1,4,7,2; two digits required. Wires blue, orange, yellow, red, green, purple. Deaf cannot verify your latest gesture. Please provide an unambiguous next instruction, ideally have Deaf relay it verbally to me.
Deaf says to Mute: I decode your A-Z gesture key. Current state is display 0, green light. Your new text reads NOW CUT PURPLE PREQQ QEIEN CUT RED PREQQ FOUR; Q and I do not match the earlier PRESS SEVEN encoding. Please confirm explicitly whether Blind should now cut purple, press keypad key 7, cut red, then press key 4, in that order.

The manual is unconditional; display and light do not alter the required sequence. My previous spelling of “PRESS SEVEN” was erroneous. I am sending Deaf a corrected, explicit instruction using the established alphabet: “YES: CUT PURPLE, PRESS SEVEN, CUT RED, PRESS FOUR, NOW.” Deaf should relay this verbally to Blind.

```text
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🖖","✌","🤛","🤏","👌","✊","🤜","🤏","🫴","✊","🫸","🫴","👉","✌","🤏","🫴","🫸","✌","🤛","🤛","🤏","🤛","✌","👊","✌","🫲","🤏","👌","✊","🤜","🤏","🫸","✌","☝","🤏","🫴","🫸","✌","🤛","🤛","🤏","🤟","🫳","✊","🫸","🤏","🫲","🫳","👋"])
```

TURN 5
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the purple wire, then press the key that wears 7,
then cut the red wire, then press the key that wears 4.
In that order, and in no other.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: I received the earlier readable sequence: CUT PURPLE, PRESS KEY SEVEN, CUT RED, PRESS KEY FOUR. Current state is display 0, green light. Please confirm verbally through Deaf that this exact sequence applies NOW at 0/green, or give the corrected sequence.
